title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (January 2027 data) + the quarterly cut — a DOUBLE release, not the triple it was proposed as, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by THIS event's own research session 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,179 bytes). The 2027 table's March row reads '18' in the Monthly column AND '18' in the 'Quarterly: Data on nonfinancial firms, derivatives, portfolio claims and liabilities' column, with '31' standing in the SEPARATE 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt' column — so 03-18 carries TWO cuts and the external-debt cut is a DISTINCT RELEASE THIRTEEN DAYS LATER on 2027-03-31 (recomputed as March 2027's last business day, matching the published cell). Page header: 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month January 2027 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-09 on the bar the six TIC siblings and mts-october-2026-11-12 set — one named Treasury primary plus independent mechanical corroboration — with the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this is the event's own session re-fetching, not the tic-monthly-2027-02-18 sweep that discovered it. Corroboration, recomputed from scratch and STATED AS WEAK: March carries no 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holiday in any year, so the holiday-aware and holiday-blind conventions are IDENTICAL here and this date discriminates nothing between them (unlike 2027-01-19, which does). The 11th business day of March 2027 is 2027-03-15, putting 03-18 at offset +3 business days — inside the page's published '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule but AT ITS OUTER EDGE. Across all 24 published 2026-27 dates the holiday-aware convention lands in-window 22 times and hits 9 exactly, independently reproducing both siblings' counts. TSY: is extended from auction schedule to release schedule on the precedent mts-august-2026-09-11, mts-october-2026-11-12 and tic-monthly-2026-09-16/10-16/11-18/12-15/2027-01-19/2027-02-18 already recorded. CONFIRMED COVERS THE SCHEDULED DATE AND NOTHING ELSE: the same page carries the standing notice 'When Federal Government offices in Washington D.C. are closed on a release date, that date will be revised after offices reopen'. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-tic-monthly-2027-02-18`, now shadowed. THE PROPOSAL'S TITLE IS CORRECTED AND ITS LIVE ALTERNATIVE IS REFUTED — that pair is this entry's output. (1) It is a DOUBLE, not 'the March triple': the '31' the proposal read as a third cut on this date sits in the separate gross-external-debt column and is its own release on 2027-03-31. That is exactly the error tic-monthly-2027-02-18 caught in ITS proposal (the annual survey standing eight days later, not inside the monthly) — the same misread of the same table, one row down. (2) The live alternative the February sibling left standing — that the Feb/Mar revision excess was always March's multi-cut release structure — CANNOT BE RIGHT, because the quarterly cut is not March's. The published table fills the quarterly column in MARCH, JUNE, SEPTEMBER AND DECEMBER, both years. A structure shared by four vintages a year cannot explain an excess found in one, and the sibling's ordinary-vintage mean of $1.67bn already contains the June/Sep/Dec quarterly-cut vintages. Note (d) killed the annual-survey mechanism; the release table kills the multi-cut mechanism; FT-tic-monthly-2027-01-19-3's post-hoc Feb/Mar exclusion now has NO SURVIVING NAMED MECHANISM, only two large Marches. (3) THE CORRIDOR IS THE WORST IN THE SERIES AND THE COLLISION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A 2027 ACCIDENT: this print publishes the session AFTER the March FOMC decision (2027-03-17, read off federalreserve.gov's own published 2027 calendar this session), on the same day as the BoJ decision, with the scored session 2027-03-19 being quad-witching. Measured on 2,990 sessions: FOMC+1 moves the 10-year 4.796bp and FOMC+2 4.860bp against 3.916bp for sessions with no FOMC within two, while equity expirations are irrelevant (quad 3.723bp, monthly opex 3.398bp, non-expiration 4.017bp, p=0.64). And the March FOMC decision has landed inside the TIC publication window in 12 of 14 years 2014-2027 — the same day in 2026 — because both dates are pinned to the same mid-month slot by their own rules. A March TIC vintage can never carry a clean tape read. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Nothing here licenses an entry.
